cells.label: Batteries — Upstream
cells.blurb: Battery minerals: lithium, nickel, cobalt, graphite and manganese ores, concentrates and intermediates, mining and refining.

cells.label: Batteries — Midstream
cells.blurb: Cathode and anode materials, lithium chemicals, electrolytes, separators, cells, packs and battery-management parts, plus manufacturing investment and capacity.

cells.label: Batteries — Downstream
cells.blurb: Stationary battery storage: deployment investment.

cells.label: Coal — Upstream
cells.blurb: Coal mining, reserves and trade in coal.

cells.label: Coal — Midstream
cells.blurb: Coal processing, briquettes, coke and handling equipment.

cells.label: Coal — Downstream
cells.blurb: Coal use and coal-fired electricity.

cells.label: Electric Grid — Upstream
cells.blurb: Copper and aluminium: ores, concentrates, cathodes and unwrought metal for grid equipment.

cells.label: Electric Grid — Midstream
cells.blurb: Cables, transformers, switchgear, converters and other grid equipment.

cells.label: Electric Grid — Downstream
cells.blurb: Grid deployment: little country-level data exists; see Grid Midstream.

cells.label: Electric Vehicles — Upstream
cells.blurb: The battery minerals EVs use and the magnet rare earths of the traction motor: trade in their ores and concentrates, and critical-minerals investment (shared with Batteries Upstream).
caveats: Electric Vehicles Upstream trade (a basket since the 2026-10 review) is the battery minerals as ores and concentrates (lithium minerals, nickel, cobalt and manganese ores, natural graphite), codes it shares with Batteries Upstream, plus the magnet rare earths of the traction motor (rare-earth compounds and metals, monazite ore), codes it shares with Wind Upstream. Each code counts fully in every sector that lists it. Steel is the larger use of nickel and manganese ore, and the lithium heading also holds other minerals.

cells.label: Electric Vehicles — Midstream
cells.blurb: Electric and hybrid vehicles, components and charging equipment, and EV production by region.
caveats: Rare-earth compounds and metals moved to the Upstream baskets in the 2026-10 basket review, so this sector's trade starts at the permanent magnet (HS 8505.11).

cells.label: Electric Vehicles — Downstream
cells.blurb: Electric-car sales, stock and sales share, and consumer purchases.

cells.label: Gas — Upstream
cells.blurb: Natural gas production, reserves and trade, including LNG.

cells.label: Gas — Midstream
cells.blurb: Pipes, compressors, liquefaction and regasification equipment.

cells.label: Gas — Downstream
cells.blurb: Gas use and gas-fired electricity.

cells.label: Geothermal — Upstream
cells.blurb: Geothermal exploration: little country-level data exists; the resource data sit in Geothermal Downstream.

cells.label: Geothermal — Midstream
cells.blurb: Geothermal equipment: little country-level data exists; the resource data sit in Geothermal Downstream.

cells.label: Geothermal — Downstream
cells.blurb: Enhanced geothermal technical potential and costs, and enhanced geothermal investment.

cells.label: Green Hydrogen — Upstream
cells.blurb: The minerals behind electrolysers: nickel and platinum-group metals.

cells.label: Green Hydrogen — Midstream
cells.blurb: Electrolyser manufacturing capacity, reported by the IEA for five economies and the EU.

cells.label: Green Hydrogen — Downstream
cells.blurb: Hydrogen use: little country-level data exists.

cells.label: Nuclear — Upstream
cells.blurb: Uranium resources, mine production and trade in uranium ores and concentrates (yellowcake).
caveats: Nuclear Upstream trade is uranium ores and concentrates (HS 2612.10) and natural uranium and its compounds (2844.10, the heading under which most yellowcake is shipped), moved from Nuclear Midstream in the 2026-10 basket review. The 2844.10 heading also holds natural uranium hexafluoride from conversion, a Midstream step with no code of its own.

cells.label: Nuclear — Midstream
cells.blurb: Enriched uranium and spent fuel, reactors and their parts, and steam-plant hardware.
caveats: Since the 2026-10 basket review Nuclear Midstream no longer includes uranium ores and yellowcake (now in Nuclear Upstream): it keeps enriched uranium, spent fuel, and reactor and steam-plant hardware.

cells.label: Nuclear — Downstream
cells.blurb: Nuclear generation and investment in nuclear power.

cells.label: Oil — Upstream
cells.blurb: Crude oil production, reserves and trade.

cells.label: Oil — Midstream
cells.blurb: Refining and handling equipment, pipes and tanks.

cells.label: Oil — Downstream
cells.blurb: Oil use and oil-fired electricity.

cells.label: Solar — Upstream
cells.blurb: The materials behind solar: trade in silicon metal, the feedstock of polysilicon, and the mining and refining of silicon, silver, copper and other minerals.
caveats: Solar Upstream trade is silicon metal only (HS 2804.69), the feedstock of polysilicon. Aluminium alloys and silicones use as much silicon metal as solar or more, so most traded silicon metal serves other uses. Silver, quartz, tellurium and copper are left out (copper is in Electric Grid Upstream).

cells.label: Solar — Midstream
cells.blurb: Polysilicon, wafers, cells, modules, inverters and related equipment, plus manufacturing investment and capacity.

cells.label: Solar — Downstream
cells.blurb: Solar generation, deployment investment and the solar resource.

cells.label: Wind — Upstream
cells.blurb: The materials behind wind: trade in the rare-earth compounds, metals and ores that magnets are made from, and the mining and refining of rare earths, copper, zinc and other minerals.
caveats: Wind Upstream trade is the raw material of the magnet rare earths: rare-earth compounds (HS 2846.90), rare-earth metals (2805.30) and monazite ore (2612.20), the same codes as in Electric Vehicles Upstream. Magnets also go into electronics and industrial motors, and the compounds heading also holds lanthanum and cerium for catalysts and glass.

cells.label: Wind — Midstream
cells.blurb: Nacelles, blades, towers, generators and cables, plus manufacturing investment and capacity.
caveats: Rare-earth compounds and metals moved to the Upstream baskets in the 2026-10 basket review, so this sector's trade starts at the permanent magnet (HS 8505.11).

cells.label: Wind — Downstream
cells.blurb: Wind generation, deployment investment and the wind resource.

cells.label: Semiconductors — Upstream
cells.blurb: Non-headline basket: unwrought gallium, germanium and indium (with niobium and vanadium), their powders and scrap.
caveats: Semiconductors Upstream trade is unwrought gallium, germanium and indium, their powders and scrap (HS 8112.92, which also holds niobium and vanadium); the Atlas sees it through the older code 8112.91. Semiconductors and LEDs take most gallium, but germanium goes mainly into fibre and infrared optics and indium into display coatings.

cells.label: Semiconductors — Midstream
cells.blurb: Non-headline basket: semiconductor devices, wafers and manufacturing equipment.
